# Model Variants

Also called: FWD, FWD-D, FWD-U

## Overview
This family defines three specific configurations for the Forward Warping Depth (FWD) framework, distinguished by their depth supervision strategy and the initialization state of the Multi-View Stereo (MVS) module. While the parent article [Monocular Depth Estimation Adaptation and Supervision](12353-monocular-depth-estimation-adaptation-and-supervision.md) establishes the general mechanism of aligning monocular priors with NeRF outputs, these variants specify how the depth prior is generated and updated during training. FWD uses a pre-trained MVS module updated end-to-end; FWD-U uses the same module but randomly initialized and unsupervised; FWD-D bypasses the MVS module entirely, using sensor depths as direct inputs.

## Shared principles
The variants share the core FWD architecture where depth maps are used to warp features from source views to target views, enabling real-time novel view synthesis. The depth estimation component is implemented via a PatchmatchNet [S1]. The training protocol involves optimizing photometric and perceptual losses [S1]. The specific distinction lies in the data pipeline and gradient flow regarding the depth estimator.

## Subtopics

### FWD
FWD is the supervised variant of the model. It utilizes a PatchmatchNet that has been pre-trained following typical MVS settings [S1]. During the end-to-end training of the NeRF, this pre-trained MVS module is not frozen; instead, it is updated jointly with the radiance field using photometric and perceptual losses [S1]. This configuration assumes the availability of multi-view consistency cues to initialize and refine the depth estimation.

### FWD-U
FWD-U represents the unsupervised depth learning variant. It shares the identical model architecture and training settings as FWD, including the use of photometric and perceptual losses [S1]. The critical difference is that the PatchmatchNet is randomly initialized and does not undergo any pre-training [S1]. Consequently, the depth estimation is learned purely from the video sequence or multi-view data without external MVS supervision or pre-trained weights.

### FWD-D
FWD-D is designed for scenarios where sensor depths are available. It takes sensor depths as additional inputs during both training and inference [S1]. Unlike FWD and FWD-U, this variant does not employ any MVS module (PatchmatchNet) because the sensor depths provide abundant geometric cues directly [S1]. This removes the need for learning depth from photometric consistency, relying instead on the provided depth measurements.

## Background
The FWD framework was introduced to achieve real-time novel view synthesis by combining forward warping with depth estimation [S1]. The model variants were evaluated on ShapeNet benchmarks, testing category-agnostic synthesis on 13 categories with 24 fixed views per instance [S1]. The evaluation protocol ensured consistent inputs and outputs across all variants to compare the impact of different depth supervision strategies [S1].
